audit_notes: Model choice: the concept's governing quantity is the rate of reflectance loss (degradation_rate); its effect on the objective is the 20-year mean solar reflectance, which I feed into the steady roof heat-flux model, so the simulation reports the heat flux to the room (relevant quantity) with the steady-state reflectance as the design input. Check of the renewal balance: dust deposition in hot arid regions 1-5 g/m2 per week; a surface erosion of ~8 um/yr removes ~20 g/m2/yr of coating, which cannot remove several hundred g/m2/yr of dust unless rain or wind scours it; in practice limewashed surfaces in dry regions settle at SR ~0.75-0.85 between renewals. Removal also leaves runoff streaks. I therefore reduce steady_state_solar_reflectance from 0.86 to 0.82 (20-year mean). Thickness budget: 300 um / 8 um/yr = 37 years, OK. Dimensionless: renewal Damkoehler number = erosion removal / deposition, ~0.5-2 depending on rain; Biot envelope 0.026. Simulation coefficient: sol-air excess (0.18*600-0.92*80)/20 = 1.72 K vs baseline 6.0 K. Baseline: aged cool paint SR 0.68, eps 0.90. Expected gain ~22 percent (roof). Mechanical: soft lime/silicate layer, low stresses; erosion is designed in. Audit passed.
